lyrics:
[Intro: chugging acoustic guitars, congas, nonsense syllables]
Doo-da-lee, doo-da-lee-dee
Doo-da-lee, doo-da-lee-dee

[Chorus: two voices in close harmony]
We see you there, Miss Abernathy
The kettle's on for more than only you
(Ooh, ooh, ooh)
Stay as you are, Miss Abernathy
The avenue is leaning on you
(Hey, hey, hey)

[Verse 1: quick, sly, guitars and bass]
She taught the whole of Elm Street how to find a middle C
She kept a tin of buttons and a list of who owed tea
She knew which kids were hungry and she never said a word
Just left a plate, and nobody heard

[Chorus: two voices in close harmony]
We see you there, Miss Abernathy
The kettle's on for more than only you
(Ooh, ooh, ooh)
Stay as you are, Miss Abernathy
The avenue is leaning on you
(Hey, hey, hey)

[Verse 2: quick, wistful]
Where did they go, the ones who knew our names?
The milkman and the crossing guard, the man who fixed the trains
The lady at the library who saved the book for you
The street is asking, and it's overdue

[Verse 3: slower, guitars soften]
The van came on a Thursday and the piano went downstairs
She waved from the back window like a queen with other cares
She left the tin of buttons on the wall beside the gate
We shared them out, we stayed up late

[Final Chorus: two voices, fuller, tambourine]
So long, so long, Miss Abernathy
The kettle's on, it's on for only you
(Ooh, ooh, ooh)
Go as you are, Miss Abernathy
The avenue will try to carry through
(Hey, hey, hey)

[Outro: guitars and nonsense syllables, fading]
Doo-da-lee, doo-da-lee-dee
